candidates.title: Ark of the Covenant guardians at Axum with cataracts and short lifespans
candidates.quote: by and large, once they are appointed guardian of the ark, they have a lifespan of about 3 years.
cites: guardians of the Ark at Axum

link.reason: Both tell of the Ark's guardians at Aksum sickening and dying quickly after appointment.
link.difference: Told firsthand from interviews; adds cataracts and a lifespan of about 3 years after appointment.

candidates.title: Falasha (Beta Israel) tradition of the Ark's journey to Ethiopia
candidates.years_text: ancient, several hundred years on the Nile
candidates.place_text: Israel; island in the Nile; Lake Tana, Ethiopia
candidates.quote: their ancestors had fled from Israel carrying the Ark. Like how they brought it to an island in the Nile River and kept it there for several hundred years.

link.reason: Both tell the Beta Israel tradition that their ancestors brought the Ark from Israel via a Nile island to Lake Tana, Ethiopia.
link.difference: Says the Ark was kept on the Nile island for several hundred years and cites the Kebra Nagast.

candidates.title: Ark moved from Axum to Lake Ziway during the Italian occupation
candidates.place_text: Axum to an island on Lake Ziway, Ethiopia
candidates.quote: um the Ethiopians say that they took the ark out of Axum. Uh and they took it to another place of safekeeping.

link.reason: Moving the Ark to Lake Ziway during the 1935-1941 Italian occupation is a distinct event; the nearest story only says the Ark is kept at Aksum.

candidates.title: Ark of the Covenant as a device that strikes people dead with fire
candidates.quote: according to the the Book of Exodus. But also, it strikes people dead with bolts of fire that come out of it.

link.reason: The Exodus account of the Ark striking people dead with fire is not any listed story; the acacia and Aksum stories are about other aspects.

candidates.title: Caliph al-Mamun's raiders find the Great Pyramid empty
candidates.quote: um Arab raiders under Calif Mamun broke in to the Great Pyramid and they found it empty.

link.reason: Al-Mamun's 9th-century break-in finding the pyramid empty is not covered; the tomb/portal story is a general theory.

candidates.title: Scans show a second Grand Gallery inside the Great Pyramid
candidates.quote: looks like there's a second Grand Gallery above it uh within within the pyramid. That shows up in scanning.

link.reason: Scans showing a second Grand Gallery inside the pyramid differ from the story of structures beneath the pyramids.

candidates.title: Great Pyramid built over hundreds of years, not in Khufu's 23-year reign
candidates.quote: More likely it's a it's a project that took hundreds of years to complete uh

link.reason: The claim that the pyramid was built over hundreds of years is distinct from the Orion correlation dating story.

candidates.title: Orion correlation and Sphinx–Leo alignment date Giza to 10,500 BC
candidates.quote: are due south on the meridian at dawn on the spring equinox is also precisely the moment that the Great Sphinx is looking at the constellation of Leo 12,500 years ago, not 4,500 years ago.

link.reason: Both date the Sphinx to 10,500 BC because it faced Leo at the spring-equinox sunrise, as Bauval and Hancock argue.
link.difference: Told by Hancock himself and ties it to the Orion belt stars lying on the meridian at the same moment.

candidates.title: Sphinx water-erosion weathering dates it to 12,500 years ago
candidates.quote: "As a geologist, when I look at the weathering patterns on this monument, it's not 4 and 1/2 thousand years old. It's more like 12 and 1/2 thousand years old."

link.reason: Both tell Schoch and West's argument that water-erosion weathering shows the Sphinx is far older.
link.difference: Quotes Schoch as a geologist and gives an age of 12,500 years.

candidates.title: Sphinx originally had a lion's head, recarved by the pharaohs
candidates.quote: Yes, originally it was a the prehistoric Sphinx was a lion.

link.reason: Both claim the Sphinx was originally a lion and its head was later recarved.
link.difference: Adds that the pharaohs recarved the head and credits no one.

candidates.title: Grandfather's 1916 graffiti at the top of the Great Pyramid
candidates.place_text: top of the Great Pyramid, south side, Giza
candidates.quote: Uh on one step down from the top, we found the name P initial P Hancock 5th of April, 1916.

link.reason: Both tell of Hancock finding his grandfather P. Hancock's name, dated 5 April 1916, near the top of the Great Pyramid.
link.difference: Places it one step down from the top on the south side and credits Philip Hancock's diaries.

candidates.title: Queen's Chamber shaft points at Orion
candidates.quote: chamber don't point at Orion, but one of the shafts of the Queen Chamber does.

link.reason: A claim that one Queen's Chamber shaft points at Orion. The Orion correlation story is about the layout of the Giza pyramids, a different claim.

candidates.title: Path of souls: the soul's leap to Orion and journey along the Milky Way
candidates.place_text: North, Central and South America; worldwide
candidates.quote: Absolutely. It is it is here it in in North America. Uh and and in Central America and in South America. The the path of souls.

link.reason: A worldwide afterlife cosmology of the soul travelling via Orion and the Milky Way. No story below covers it.

candidates.title: Ptolemy on the soul's ascension through Orion's Belt
candidates.quote: he's saying that the, you know, soul's ascension path is through Orion's Belt.

link.reason: Ptolemy's text on the soul ascending through Orion's Belt is a specific document. No story below matches it, and telling 3 is a general cosmology.

candidates.title: Gudea of Sumer given temple plans in a dream
candidates.quote: King Judaea of Sumeria saying that in a dream he was given this lapis lazuli,

link.reason: Gudea receiving temple plans in a dream. The Sumerian stories below are about king lists and astronomy, not this.

candidates.title: Göbekli Tepe Pillar 43 as a sky map of 12,500 years ago
candidates.years_text: c. 12,500 years ago; enclosure dated 11,600 years ago
candidates.quote: find is that that is very persuasively an astronomical diagram of the sky at the summer solstice 12 and 1/2 thousand years ago.

link.reason: Pillar 43 read as a sky map. The Göbekli Tepe stories below are about chalices, origins of civilization and Hancock's lost civilization in general.

candidates.title: Hamlet's Mill on ancient knowledge of precession
candidates.quote: very ancient very early knowledge of of precession.

link.reason: The book Hamlet's Mill and ancient knowledge of precession. No story below covers it.

candidates.title: Followers of Horus secret societies preserving knowledge from the First Time
candidates.quote: that these were secret societies which were entrusted with preserving information from what they call the first time and passing it down to future generations.

link.reason: The Followers of Horus as secret societies preserving knowledge. This is distinct from the general lost-civilization stories and from the Irish monks.

candidates.title: Civilizations switching on at the same time around 3000 BC
candidates.quote: that's exactly the same period that the engine of the Indus Valley civilization was switched on in what is now Pakistan

link.reason: The claim that civilizations started at the same time around 3000 BC. The Indus discovery story is about railway workers finding the sites, a different story.

candidates.title: Atlantis date given to Solon by the priests of Sais
candidates.years_text: c. 600 BC telling; c. 9600 BC event
candidates.place_text: Temple of Neith, Sais, Nile Delta, Egypt
candidates.quote: gives that date because the Egyptian priests who read the hieroglyphs on the wall of the temple of Neith at Sais in the Delta to Solon and translated it for him.

link.reason: Both tell of the priests at the Temple of Neith at Sais giving Solon the Atlantis account.
link.difference: Adds that the priests read the hieroglyphs on the temple wall and translated them, and gives the dates c. 600 BC and c. 9600 BC.

candidates.title: Troy found to be real in the late 19th century
candidates.quote: the the city of Troy did not exist and then late 19th century we figured out, "Oh, there actually was a city

link.reason: Both are about Troy being shown to be real in the late 19th century, credited to Schliemann.
link.difference: Places the discovery in the late 19th century and stresses that Troy had been thought not to exist; does not mention Anatolia.

candidates.title: Pablo Amaringo's flying saucers as vehicles for the spirit world
candidates.quote: matter-of-factly, he he said, "Oh, well, those are vehicles for entering and leaving the spirit world."

link.reason: Both are Hancock relaying Amaringo's statement that flying saucers are vehicles for entering and leaving the spirit world.
link.difference: Dates it loosely to the 1990s-2000s rather than 2005, and credits the books Supernatural and Visionary.

candidates.title: Extended-state DMT trials yield encounters with sentient others
candidates.place_text: Imperial College London; University of California San Diego
candidates.quote: minutes. And And those volunteers are all coming back with reports of encounters with sentient others.

link.reason: This covers the recent extended-state DMT trials across several sites, Imperial and UCSD, and their volunteers' entity reports. The nearest stories are narrower: the 2015 Gallimore–Strassman proposal and Imperial's 30-minute extension.

candidates.title: Graham Hancock's yage experience of a communicating presence
candidates.quote: in in every way and again this sense of a a presence and of and and of communication.

link.reason: Hancock's yage experience of a communicating presence is a different session from his 2003 ayahuasca vision of flying saucers and alien faces.

candidates.title: Kary Mullis saw an alien
candidates.quote: Kary Mullis saw an alien, too.

link.reason: No story covers Kary Mullis's alien encounter.

candidates.title: Curse of King Tut's tomb
candidates.quote: like anybody that you know you had a couple people try to x-ray it and then they sort of die mysteriously.

link.reason: No story covers the curse of Tutankhamun's tomb.

candidates.title: Uranium at Skinwalker Ranch
candidates.quote: a modern context on Skinwalker Ranch, they say that there's like a lot of uranium around.

link.reason: The claim about uranium at Skinwalker Ranch is distinct from the stories about the ranch's curse legend, cattle mutilations or the host's visits there.

candidates.title: UFOs show up around US nuclear bases
candidates.quote: about how UFOs consistently show up around nuclear bases all over the US.

link.reason: Both are Robert Hastings' documentation of UFOs consistently appearing at US nuclear bases.
link.difference: A brief summary that gives no interview numbers.

candidates.title: Phenomena showing up around nuclear bases
candidates.quote: showing up around nuclear bases, that's that's that's interesting.

link.reason: Hancock's general remark that phenomena appear around nuclear bases is a broad claim with no source. The nearest story is the narrower Hastings interview collection.

candidates.title: Oppenheimer's rumored 'first atom bomb in modern history' remark and Vedic death weapons
candidates.quote: a student of his was rumored to come up to him and said, um you know, "You've created the the first atom bomb, you know, how do you feel?" And he said, "I've created the first atom bomb in modern history."

link.reason: Both tell the apocryphal story of Oppenheimer saying he made the first atom bomb 'in modern history'.
link.difference: Adds the link to Vedic death weapons and credits the Bhagavad Gita and the Vedas.

candidates.title: Tayos Cave metallic library of alien artifacts
candidates.quote: at the edge of Ecuador, this this cave that they they claim to have ancient, what feels like an alien metallic artifacts. It's like it was a library actually of these books.

link.reason: This is lore about the Tayos Cave itself, a supposed metallic library of alien artifacts. The nearest story is Armstrong's 1975 expedition, which is one event at the cave, not the cave legend.

candidates.title: Neil Armstrong's 1975 Tayos Cave expedition with BBC film crew
candidates.place_text: Tayos Cave, Ecuador (edge of the Amazon)
candidates.quote: And then in the next expedition he goes on has nothing to do with space. It's to this cage at the edge of the Amazon which is rumored to have these sort of alien artifacts and he brings this BBC film crew in with him in 1975.

link.reason: Both tell of Neil Armstrong taking a BBC film crew to the Tayos cave at the edge of the Amazon in Ecuador in 1975.
link.difference: Frames it as Armstrong's next expedition after the moon and says nothing of von Däniken.

candidates.title: Guide's son claims his father led Armstrong down the wrong path
candidates.quote: They didn't find it. But I'm in touch with this guy who claims that his father led Neil Armstrong down the wrong path.

link.reason: The claim by the guide's son that his father led Armstrong down the wrong path is a narrower incident inside the 1975 expedition story, not the expedition itself.

candidates.title: Ice Age Sahara as origin of Egyptian civilization
candidates.quote: I think if we want to get into the origins of ancient Egyptian civilization, we're going to have to start looking at what the Sahara was doing during the Ice Age.

link.reason: The nearest story ties a lost civilization to Egypt in general. This telling makes a distinct claim that the Ice Age Sahara was where Egyptian civilization began.

candidates.title: Richat Structure as Plato's Atlantis
candidates.place_text: Richat Structure (Eye of the Sahara), Mauritania
candidates.quote: I get that the ring structure resembles how Plato described Atlantis.

link.reason: Both tell the theory that the Richat Structure in Mauritania was Plato's Atlantis, credited to Jimmy Corsetti.
link.difference: Told by Graham Hancock, who grants the ring resembles Plato's description but goes on to qualify the claim.

candidates.title: Atlantis as a multi-site Ice Age civilization
candidates.place_text: North America, Azores, Sahara, Amazon, submerged continental shelves
candidates.quote: but I think it was more than one place.

link.reason: Hancock's claim that Atlantis spanned several sites is a distinct theory. The Mid-Atlantic, Richat and Thera stories each place Atlantis in a single spot.

candidates.title: Lidar reveals lost Amazon cities and geometric earthworks
candidates.quote: where they are looking, they're finding extraordinary mysteries. They're They're finding that the Amazon was once populated by tens of millions of people, that they were able to feed themselves, that there were huge cities in the Amazon with permanent populations, that there are enormous geometrical earthworks, precisely very precise on an enormous scale, which actually can only be seen in full form from from an aerial view.

link.reason: This is a broad claim about lidar showing Amazon cities, large populations and earthworks. The nearest story covers one lidar-detected pyramid, which is narrower.

candidates.title: 15th-16th century explorers' accounts of Amazon cities
candidates.quote: that you've heard 16th, 15th century explorers seeing these things driving your research, and then you corroborating those stories.

link.reason: Early explorers' accounts of Amazon cities are a distinct historical claim. No story below covers them.

candidates.title: 23,000-year-old human footprints in New Mexico
candidates.quote: And those footprints in New Mexico, 23,000 year-old human footprints in New Mexico, which are interspersed with footprints of mammoths and mastodons and giant sloths and all the extinct megafauna of the Ice Age, they actually have been dated.

link.reason: Both tell of Ice Age human footprints in North America, dated to about 22,000 to 23,000 years ago and shown by Hancock.
link.difference: Names New Mexico, says 23,000 rather than 22,000 years, and adds the megafauna tracks found among them.

candidates.title: Evidence of humans in the Americas 130,000 years ago
candidates.quote: even much older evidence for humans in the Americas going back as much as 130,000 years into the past, 10 times older than the supposed first habitation of the Americas

link.reason: A claim that humans were in the Americas 130,000 years ago is a separate claim from the 23,000-year-old footprints.

candidates.title: Alvarez asteroid impact theory and the Chicxulub crater
candidates.quote: But it still wasn't accepted until they found the crater. These are These are which is the Chicxulub crater, deeply buried in the Gulf of Mexico.

link.reason: Both tell of the Alvarez theory that an asteroid or comet impact killed the dinosaurs, with the buried Chicxulub crater as the evidence. The teller is the same, Graham Hancock.
link.difference: Stresses that the theory was not accepted until the crater was found, and places the crater in the Gulf of Mexico rather than the Yucatan.

candidates.title: Younger Dryas comet impact 12,800 years ago
candidates.quote: of a disintegrating comet, the the debris trail of a disintegrating comet roughly 12,800 years ago. That's the Younger Dryas impact hypothesis.

link.reason: This telling states the general Younger Dryas comet impact hypothesis. The nearest stories each make a narrower or different claim: Napier's Taurid link, the 2007 paper, and Rogan's flood and civilization-reset cosmology.

candidates.title: Lockheed VP Jim Ryder: the veil thinning as weakening magnetosphere
candidates.quote: this guy Jim Ryder, this VP of space systems there saying that the vent the fail sorry, the veil is thinning and that that is literally the magnetosphere of the earth which is weakening right now.

link.reason: The story about Jim Ryder is about his talk 'The Garment of God' as a document. This telling is one specific claim credited to him, that the veil thinning is the weakening magnetosphere, so it is at a narrower grain.
